result.topic_en: The page records formulas 63) and 64), double sums of logarithmic terms over $(2nt+p)^2$ or $(nt+p)^2$ for odd and even n, and then proves Abel's theorem on the limit of a power series at r=1 by summation by parts.
result.transcription:
63). $n$ impar $= -\sum_{1,2n-1}^{p}\sum_{-\infty,\infty}^{t}\frac{\lg\lg\frac{p\,m\pi}{n}^2}{(2nt+p)^2}$ ; \quad $n$ par. $= -\sum_{-\infty,\infty}^{t}\sum_{1,n-1}^{p}\frac{\lg\lg\frac{p\,m\pi}{n}^2}{(nt+p)^2}$
64). $n$ impar $= \sum_{1,2n-1}^{p}\sum_{-\infty,\infty}^{t}\frac{\lg 4\cos\frac{p\,m\pi}{n}^2}{(2nt+p)^2}$ , \quad $n$ par $= \sum_{1,n-1}^{p}\sum_{-\infty,\infty}^{t}\frac{\lg.4\cos\frac{p\,m\pi}{n}^2}{(nt+p)^2}$
[ Formulae 63) [-64)-] partem habe{+n+}t infinitam, nisi $n\equiv 0 \bmod.4$ \} formula 64 si $n$ formae {+est+} $(4\nu+2)$ ]

Convergentia summae
$a_0+a_1+a_2+a_3+\dots$
postulat, ut, data quantitate quamvis parva $\varepsilon$, assignari possit terminus $a_n$, a quo summa usque ad terminum quemvis [-extensa-] $a_m$ extensa, numerisatur[?] valorem absolutum ipso $\varepsilon$ minorem.
Jam posito {+brevitatis gratia+}
$[-\mathcal{E}-]\ \varepsilon_{n+1}=a_{n+1}$
$\varepsilon_{n+2}=a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}$
$\varepsilon_{n+3}=a_{n+1}+a_{n+2}+a_{n+3}$ &c
$\cdot\ \cdot\ \cdot\ \cdot$
functio $f(r)=a_0+a_1r+a_2r^2+\dots$ facile sub hac forma exhibetur:
$f(r)=a_0+a_1r+\dots a_nr^n+\varepsilon_{n+1}r^{n+1}+(\varepsilon_{n+2}-\varepsilon_{n+1})r^{n+2}+(\varepsilon_{n+3}-\varepsilon_{n+2})r^{n+3}+\dots$
$=a_0+a_1r+\dots a_nr^n+\varepsilon_{n+1}(r^{n+1}-r^{n+2})+\varepsilon_{n+2}(r^{n+2}-r^{n+3})+\varepsilon_{n+3}(r^{n+3}-r^{n+4})+\dots$
unde patet, convergente $r$ versus limitem 1 functionem $f(r)$ tandem quavis quantitate minus a valore seriei $a_0+a_1+\dots a_n$ distare
Summa terminorum altioris gradus quam $n$ quum sint $\varepsilon_{n+1},\varepsilon_{n+2}\dots$ ex hyp omnes omisso signo $<\varepsilon$ differentiaeque $r^{n+1}-r^{n+2},\dots$ positivae, manifesto evadit quantitate absoluta
$<\varepsilon(r^{n+1}-r^{n+2})+\varepsilon(r^{n+2}-r^{n+3})\dots$
$<\varepsilon r^{n+1}$
summa autem terminorum non altioris gradus quam $n$ est functio algebraica ipsius $r$, quam constat appropinquando $r$ ad limitem 1, summae
$a_0+a_1+\dots+a_n$
quantumvis admoveri posse, unde patet, appropinquante {+($r$ ad limitem 1)+} differentiam functionis $f(r)$ a valore seriei $a_0+a_1+\dots$ infra quantitatem quamvis datam descendere

items.english: Formula 63) has an infinite part unless n ≡ 0 mod 4; formula 64 does so if n is of the form 4ν+2.

items.english: Hence it is evident that, as r approaches the limit 1, the difference of the function f(r) from the value of the series a_0+a_1+... falls below any given quantity.

items.english: From this theorem, which the eminent Dirichlet just now (14 Sept. 1852), when the preceding had already been written, pointed out is to be attributed to the eminent Abel, it is easily deduced ——
